relevant_gaps.gap: ForecasterDirectMultiVariate on wide data (target list) was never run end to end. Not one test in tests/tests_mcp mentions it; it only appears in the schema golden. Axis a saw it only as an alternative the profile lists.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: The profile offers it as an alternative and the schema describes it as 'one series predicted from several', but no tool argument chooses which series is predicted. assistant.py:1432 always predicts target[0], the first column of the target list, and only plan's explanation says so. A client that wants to forecast 'sales from price and traffic' has to know to put sales first in profile's target list, and neither SKILL.md nor the tool descriptions tell it. The behaviour of backtest metrics, files.predictions, forecast with exog_path, compare (baseline? candidate rows?), the cost (one estimator per step) and get_code for this forecaster is all unobserved over stdio.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Use a_happy_path/data/multi_wide.csv. Run profile(target=[a,b,c]), then plan(forecaster='ForecasterDirectMultiVariate', steps=12), create_cv, backtest, forecast, compare(candidates=[{DMV},{ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries}]) and get_code. Check: which level the summary, metrics and predictions name; whether the multi-series metric rows (average, weighted, pooling) still appear for one level; whether reordering target changes the predicted series; whether cost.estimator_fits counts steps; and whether the get_code script reproduces the numbers. Also try it with exog and an exog_path, and with an interval.

relevant_gaps.gap: CSV encodings and dialects outside UTF-8 were never tried (axis b listed this as not covered): cp1252 or latin-1 accents, UTF-16 with a BOM (Excel's 'Unicode text' export), CRLF line endings, quoted headers holding the separator ("Sales, units"), and headers with surrounding whitespace.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: These are the most common shapes of a real user's export (Excel on Windows, Spanish or European locales). SKILL.md promises data_unreadable for 'not UTF-8'. The silent alternative would be mojibake in column or category names, a target that no longer matches what the user typed, or CRLF leaving '\r' in the last column (a target or exog name 'y\r', or a numeric column turned into text). In each case the agent cannot recover by following the hint.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Generate small variants of b_hard_data/data/base.csv: (1) cp1252 with 'Año' and 'Ventas €' in the header and accented category values; (2) UTF-16LE with a BOM and a tab separator; (3) CRLF with ',' and with ';' plus decimal ','; (4) a header '"date","Sales, units"'; (5) ' y ' with spaces. For each, run profile with the target named as the user would type it, then plan, backtest and get_code. Check the error code and hint (data_unreadable vs invalid_argument on target), whether column names come back exactly, and whether the standalone script reads the file the same way (encoding, quoting).

relevant_gaps.gap: Progress and cancellation over stdio on real (not monkeypatched) long runs. Specifically: the 5 s heartbeat text for a backtest, a forecast and a compare candidate ('ForecasterStats: running (35 s)'); whether a call queued behind a long run gets any progress while it waits its turn; how long a cancelled compare takes to free the server ('waits for the candidate in progress, skips the rest'); and whether get_failure and describe_object answer during a compare.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: Many MCP clients put a request timeout of about 60 s on each call, reset only by progress notifications. A queued non-read call that gets no heartbeat would time out on the client while the server still runs it later, which leaves an orphan object or duplicate work. tests_mcp only checks the heartbeat with a patched HEARTBEAT and sleep, and checks compare cancellation only by 'no comparison registered', never by timing. Axis d checked only list_objects and get_code during a backtest, and V26's verdict shows a cancelled backtest still blocks profile for more than 20 s.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Build a backtest of ForecasterStats with about 10 folds, or RandomForest with refit=true and about 20 folds, on monthly data so it lasts 20 to 40 s on 4 CPUs. Pass progress_callback to: (a) the backtest itself; (b) a plan or profile call started 1 s later; (c) a compare of 3 slow candidates cancelled after the first 'started' event, followed by profile, measuring when it answers and whether the skipped candidates leave files in --output-dir. In parallel, call get_failure and describe_object during (c). Record the message format and timestamps of the notifications.

relevant_gaps.gap: Dates that are not plain naive ISO dates: timezone-aware or DST offsets ('2024-03-31T01:00:00+01:00' next to '+02:00'), hourly or sub-daily data, month-end dates (ME), quarterly data. Also test_size or initial_train_size given as a date that falls on a weekend for business-day data, or between timestamps. Axis b did not cover test_size dates on business-day or irregular indexes.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: SKILL.md tells the agent to pass the ISO date the test set starts at. A user who says 'from June 1st' gives a Saturday on business-day data. A server that rejects it without saying why, or shifts it silently, misplaces the HoldoutEvaluationNotice dates. Mixed-offset timestamps are the default export of many energy and IoT systems; they can become an object column (exog 'date') or fail with raw pandas text. Calendar features ('hour', 'weekend') and the seasonal naive baseline period on hourly data are also unobserved.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Use b_hard_data/data/business_days.csv. Call forecast(test_size='<a Saturday>') and create_cv(initial_train_size='<a Sunday>'), then compare the dates in the notice and the files. Generate an hourly series with tz offsets that cross DST, a UTC 'Z' series, a month-end series and a quarterly series. On each, run profile, plan (default calendar_features), create_cv, compare (baseline name and period) and forecast. Check the detected freq, the notices, the error codes and hints, and the forecast dates.

relevant_gaps.gap: data_changed beyond profile, backtest and forecast (the only tools tests_mcp covers for it): compare, create_cv and get_code after the data file changes, an exog file that changes between two forecast calls, and false positives (a touch with the same content, or an atomic rewrite with identical bytes).
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: SKILL.md's 'Data problems' flow has the agent write corrected copies, and users edit files between calls. If compare runs silently on new content, its numbers no longer match the profile. If a mere mtime change (an editor saving without changes, or a sync client) raises data_changed, the agent is pushed to re-profile, which drops every id. Axis e reports seeing data_changed once but has no script, so which check it is (mtime, size, hash) is unknown to the audit.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Run profile, plan and create_cv on a copy of monthly.csv. Then: (1) os.utime only, and call backtest, compare and forecast; (2) rewrite the same bytes through a temp file and os.replace; (3) append one row and call create_cv, compare and get_code(backtest_id); (4) forecast with exog_path, change one future value, and forecast again. Record which calls raise data_changed, with which field and hint, and whether any call returns results from the new content without a notice.

relevant_gaps.gap: Long-format multi-series data with realistic hard cases. These were never run (axis b not_covered): series ids with leading zeros ('001') in the data and in exog_future.csv, one very short series among long ones, series that end on different dates, and an exog_future file missing a series or holding an extra one.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: Store, SKU and sensor ids are often zero-padded. If pandas reads them as integers in one file and not the other, forecast with exog_path fails with 'no row for' errors, or predictions are labelled '1' while the user knows '001'. For unaligned ends, the SKILL does not say what the forecast horizon starts at per series. These are the common multi-series datasets an agent will meet.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: Generate long data with series_id '001','002','010' (one of them 20 rows long, one ending 3 months earlier), plus temperature exog and an exog_future.csv with the same zero-padded ids. Variants: ids written without padding in the future file, one series missing, one extra. Run profile, plan, create_cv (cost, notices), backtest (per-series metrics: do the ids keep their zeros?), forecast with exog_path (dates per series, error codes and field) and get_code (does the script read ids as str?).

relevant_gaps.gap: Object store limits in a normal long session: how many objects one compare registers (candidate plans?), whether the default --max-objects 256 or a small --max-memory-mb evicts ids the agent still holds (the profile, links.best_plan_id, a comparison_id needed by get_failure or get_code), and an object larger than --max-memory-mb by itself. Axis d covered only --max-objects 2; size-based eviction was not run.
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: Axis d already saw compare return a links.best_plan_id that was already evicted with --max-objects 1. If compare registers one plan per candidate, a few 30-candidate compares hit 256 objects and the early profile and plan disappear mid-conversation. The agent then gets unknown_id 'removed ... create it again' with no clue why, and SKILL.md's 'when an id was removed to keep the server within its limits' gives no idea of the budget. Size-based eviction of a big profile or forecast could also return an id that is unusable on the next call.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: After compare with N=5, 20 and 40 Ridge candidates (refit=false, cheap), count the objects per kind with list_objects. Start the server with --max-memory-mb 1 and profile a 100k-row synthetic file, then call plan on the returned id immediately. Run a loop of compares with --max-objects 20 and check that best_plan_id, comparison_id (for get_failure and get_code) and the cv stay usable. Inspect the unknown_id details for any limit figures.

relevant_gaps.gap: compare argument interactions and summary size limits: an explicit asymmetric compare interval with default candidates that include ForecasterStats (which rejects asymmetric intervals), the axis d versus axis e disagreement on it ('rejected' vs 'no baseline'), baseline=false versus 'no baseline' in the trust ranking, summary truncation at 20,000 characters with files.summary (never reached), and get_failure edge cases ('no failed candidate named None', get_failure(comparison_id) with no candidate when exactly one failed).
relevant_gaps.why_relevant: SKILL.md says that with an asymmetric interval there is no baseline. comparison.py:610 confirms 'No baseline', yet axis d wrote that an asymmetric compare interval is 'rejected', so the real behaviour per path (argument vs plan interval, Stats candidate present) is unclear. A large candidate list is the obvious way an agent fills the leaderboard and reaches the 20k cut; whether summary_truncated comes with a readable files.summary and the leaderboard file has not been observed. The get_failure 'None' text was noted but never filed.
relevant_gaps.how_to_probe: On monthly data, run compare(cv_id, interval=[0.05, 0.8]) with no candidates (Stats among the defaults) and with baseline true and false, and read the rows, failures and summary. Then compare 120 Ridge candidates with long names (lags 1..60 x two transformers, refit=false) and check summary length, summary_truncated, files.summary and the leaderboard. Finally call get_failure(comparison_id) without a candidate on a comparison with zero failures and with exactly one failure, plus get_failure with a backtest's failure_id after the backtest is evicted.

explored.coverage:
Black-box gap round. I drove the server only over stdio with _client.py, deciding every call from SKILL.md and tool_catalog.md. Scripts and data are in /home/user/skforecast-ai/reports/mcp-blackbox-audit/g_gaps/: make_data.py writes 5 small CSVs to data/, and g_01 to g_05 are the finding scripts. Each script ran twice, gave REPRODUCED and exited 0 both times. They pass ruff and contain no en or em dashes. I read tests/tests_mcp only at the end. None of g-01..g-05 is covered there, and none duplicates V01..V34.

Gap 1, ForecasterDirectMultiVariate on wide data (multi_wide.csv), behaved CORRECTLY on these points:
- The plan says which series it predicts ("It predicts 'store_a', the first series of the target"). Reordering the target list changes the predicted series consistently in the plan, the metrics and the predictions.
- Metrics and predictions name that single level, and the metrics have no average, weighted or pooling rows.
- cost.estimator_fits = steps (12), and the backtest summary explains one estimator per step.
- An interval gives lower_bound and upper_bound columns.
- With an exogenous column, the plan gets FutureExogNotice. forecast without exog_path is a clean invalid_argument; with exog_path it works; test_size works.
- compare mixing DMV and RecursiveMultiSeries candidates is rejected with a clear invalid_argument ("Compare each family in its own call").
- A default compare from a DMV strategy plan leaves that plan out with a UserWarning that says why.
- The get_code script of the backtest reproduces the numbers.
- Minor: the summary says "Results (average across series)" for one series, and compare says "No baseline ... multi-series or mu[ltivariate]" although DMV predicts one series.

Gap 2, encodings and dialects (variants of base.csv), all CORRECT:
- cp1252 with 'Año' and 'Ventas €', and UTF-16 with a BOM (tab or comma), give data_unreadable with a UTF-8 hint, as SKILL.md documents.
- CRLF with ',', and CRLF with ';' plus decimal ',', run through backtest and get_code. The script keeps sep and decimal.
- A quoted header '"Sales, units"' works end to end.
- Headers with surrounding spaces give invalid_argument on target, listing the exact names (' y '). Passing ' y ' then works.

Gap 3, progress and cancellation on real long runs:
- The heartbeat works for a ForecasterStats backtest (about 20 s): 'ForecasterStats: running (5 s)', then 10, 15, 20 s, with growing fractional progress and total None.
- A RandomForest backtest gets 'ForecasterRecursive: running (5 s)'.
- A plan call queued 1 s behind a 20 s backtest gets no progress notification and answers when the backtest ends. This is documented ("the others wait their turn"), so I did not file it.
- A compare of 3 Stats candidates cancelled at the first 'stats_0: started' event: profile answered 20.6 s later (as documented), list_objects answered at once, and no files of the cancelled compare were left in --output-dir.
- During a compare, describe_object and get_failure answered at once. Exception: the first get_code of the session (g-05).

Gap 4, dates:
- Business days: forecast(test_size=<Saturday>) gives a clear invalid_argument ("test set has 2 observations but steps is 10"). A weekday date gives a correct HoldoutEvaluationNotice. create_cv(initial_train_size=<Sunday>) starts the test on the next Monday.
- Mixed +01:00/+02:00 offsets across DST give a clear profile error with a hint.
- UTC 'Z' hourly, naive hourly, month-end (ME), quarter-start (QS-OCT) and quarter-end (QE-DEC) data all ran correctly:
  - freq detected;
  - calendar features hour/day_of_week/weekend for hourly data;
  - a seasonal naive baseline in compare;
  - forecast dates correct, with +00:00 kept.
- An exog future file with naive dates on UTC data gives a clean invalid_argument on exog_path. One with Europe/Madrid offsets is converted correctly.

Gap 5, data_changed, CORRECT:
- os.utime alone and an atomic rewrite of identical bytes give no false positive for backtest, compare or forecast.
- After appending a row, backtest, compare, forecast(test_size) and a backtest of a cv created after the change all give data_changed (field data_path, hint "Call profile again", nothing run).
- create_cv, plan and refine_plan still build objects on the stale profile without a notice, but no numbers come out of them.
- get_code(backtest) returns the script without a warning that the file changed.
- An exog file changed between two forecasts is simply re-read, as expected.

Gap 6, long data with hard cases:
- Letter ids work.
- An exog_future missing a series gives a clean invalid_argument naming it.
- Series ending early get a DataProfileWarning naming them.
- Numeric or zero-padded ids fail every run (g-02), and a short series vanishes from the backtest (g-03).

Gap 7, object store, CORRECT:
- A compare registers 2 objects (the comparison and the best plan) whatever the number of candidates (5, 20, 40).
- list_objects reports max_objects, max_memory_mb and removed.
- With --max-objects 20 over 12 compares, best_plan_id, comparison_id (get_failure, get_code), the cv and the touched profile and plan stayed usable.
- get_failure(failure_id) still works after the failed object's neighbours are evicted with --max-objects 4.
- --max-memory-mb 1 evicted nothing: a profile of a 100k-row file, then plan, and a backtest of 1600 folds; all ids stayed usable.

Gap 8, compare arguments:
- An asymmetric compare interval [0.05, 0.8] (and the same interval from the plan) runs. The summary says "No baseline: ... symmetric intervals only". The default ForecasterStats candidate fails and is ranked last with a clear error.
- baseline=false just drops that sentence.
- 120 Ridge candidates with 90-character names gave a 12,132-character summary, so no truncation. The leaderboard has all 121 rows; the 42 failed candidates are ranked last with their error.
- get_failure(comparison_id) without a candidate, when failures exist, returns invalid_argument "has no failed candidate named None. Failed candidates: [...]". The list lets the agent recover; it leaks a Python None and has a null hint. I noted it and did not file it.
explored.not_covered:
- Foundation models: chronos is not installed and there is no network.
- Summary truncation at 20,000 characters: not reached even with 120 long-named candidates, since the summary lists a limited number of rows.
- Size-based eviction (--max-memory-mb 1): never triggered, because objects appear to hold little memory. No id was evicted by size, so the behaviour of an object larger than the limit stays unobserved.
- A client with a real request timeout: the silence of a queued call was measured, but no timeout or orphan object was triggered.
- Data files: latin-1 accents only in category values (not in the header), and day-first dates in exog_future of long data.
- Gap 6 cases not run past the KeyError of numeric ids (g-02): zero-padded ids in exog_future.csv, and future-file variants with numeric ids.
- Cancelling a compare during a queued (not running) call.
- get_failure while a compare that has already failed one candidate is still running.
- DMV with refit=true and its cost.
- Why the first get_code of a session blocks (g-05): seen only during ForecasterStats runs. During a RandomForest backtest it answered in 1.6 s. The cause (plausibly an import or JIT lock) is unknown from the outside.

findings.title: ForecasterDirectMultiVariate keeps the estimator chosen for the pooled series (LGBMRegressor, '288 observations'); its backtest model learns nothing and repeats the same predictions in every fold
findings.input: Wide data a_happy_path/data/multi_wide.csv (3 monthly series x 96 dates). profile(target=['store_a','store_b','store_c']) -> plan(steps=12, forecaster='ForecasterDirectMultiVariate') -> create_cv(plan_id) -> backtest(cv_id) -> compare(cv_id, candidates=[DMV with the plan estimator, DMV with Ridge]). Control: profile of store_a alone.
findings.observed:
- The plan keeps 'Estimator: LGBMRegressor' with the reason 'A gradient boosting model is preferred for a dataset of this size (288 observations)', the three series pooled.
- DMV trains on one row per date: 96 dates, 67 in the first training window.
- The same series alone gets 'Estimator: Ridge. A linear model is preferred because the dataset is small (96 observations < 250)'.
- The default backtest predictions are identical in every fold (62.421, 62.675, 62.688, 62.504, ... in folds 0, 1 and 2): LGBM found no split, so the model is a constant per step.
- Backtest MASE is 3.587. DMV with Ridge on the same folds gets 0.488.
- No notice at plan, create_cv or backtest.
findings.expected: For DMV, the estimator rule should use the rows DMV actually trains on (one per date). That gives Ridge, as for the series alone. At least, a notice should say the training set is too small for the gradient boosting model. The plan should not give a 288-observation reason, and the backtest should not repeat a constant model.
findings.agent_impact: An agent following SKILL.md leaves the estimator to the rules, backtests the DMV plan the user asked for and reports MASE 3.59 as its accuracy. It concludes that DMV forecasts much worse than the naive reference, while the same forecaster with the rule's own small-data estimator scores 0.49. The summary's reason is false for this forecaster, so the agent repeats it to the user.

findings.title: Long data whose series ids are numbers ('001', '002', '010' or 1, 2, 10) fails every backtest, forecast and compare with execution_failed KeyError: 1, and the zero padding is lost
findings.input: g_gaps/data/stores_padded_ids.csv: columns store,date,sales; store ids '001','002','010'; 96 monthly rows each. profile(target='sales', series_id_column='store') -> plan(steps=12) -> create_cv -> backtest / forecast / compare; get_code(plan) run standalone. Control: the same values with ids 'S01','S02','S10'.
findings.observed:
- The profile names the series '1', '2', '10': the zeros are gone. Profile and create_cv give no notice.
- backtest and forecast return {code: execution_failed, message: 'The generated script failed with KeyError. ...', field: null, hint: null}.
- compare returns all_candidates_failed.
- get_failure shows 'KeyError: 1' raised in skforecast _forecaster_recursive_multiseries.py (encoding_mapping_[series_name_k]).
- The get_code script fails the same way when run standalone.
- Plain integer ids ('1','2','10') fail the same way, with or without exogenous columns. Letter ids run fine.
findings.expected: Series ids kept as the text of the file ('001', ...), and the runs working as they do with letter ids. Failing that, an error before anything runs that names the series ids as the cause, with a field (series_id_column) and a hint.
findings.agent_impact: Store, SKU and sensor ids are very often numeric or zero-padded. In that case the whole workflow dead-ends: SKILL.md says to call get_failure, whose traceback is a skforecast internal KeyError with no clue that the ids are the cause. The agent cannot propose the fix (ids as text), and it reports '1'/'2' to a user who knows the stores as '001'/'002'.

findings.title: A series too short for the plan is silently left out of a multi-series backtest (empty row, average over the others, no notice), then forecast of the same plan fails on it
findings.input: g_gaps/data/stores_one_short.csv: long data with stores S01 and S10 (96 months) and S02 (the last 20 months). profile(target='sales', series_id_column='store') -> plan(steps=12) -> create_cv(plan_id) -> backtest(cv_id) -> forecast(plan_id).
findings.observed:
- Profile and plan only say 'Short series: only 20 observations. Results may be unreliable...', without naming the series. create_cv has no notice.
- The backtest succeeds with only MetricReferenceNotice and MetricUnitNotice. Its summary reads 'Results (average across series): ... mean_absolute_scaled_error: 0.4715'.
- The metrics file has an all-NaN row for S02. The average, weighted_average and pooling rows cover S01 and S10 only. The predictions file has no S02 rows.
- forecast of the same plan then fails: insufficient_data "... ('S02': 20), so it cannot be trained on them".
findings.expected: The profile or plan should name the short series. create_cv or the backtest should say that S02 is not forecast in any fold, and that a forecast of this plan will fail for it. The summary should not present an average 'across series' that silently excludes one.
findings.agent_impact: Following SKILL.md (no baseline with several series, so read the per-series rows and name the worst), the agent reports the plan's accuracy across the three stores and cannot name the worst, which is the one never forecast. It only learns of the problem at forecast time, after presenting the backtest as the measure of a plan that cannot forecast that store.

findings.title: forecast(test_size=<ISO date with a time zone>) is an internal_error TypeError ('do not retry'), on tz-aware and naive data alike
findings.input: g_gaps/data/hourly_utc.csv: hourly, dates written '2024-03-20T00:00:00Z'. profile(target='load') -> plan(steps=24, estimator='Ridge') -> forecast(plan_id, test_size='2024-04-09T00:00:00Z'), then '...+00:00', then '2024-04-09'. Also create_cv(initial_train_size='2024-04-03T00:00:00Z'). The same calls on a naive copy of the file.
findings.observed:
- On the UTC data, test_size '2024-04-09T00:00:00Z' and '2024-04-09T00:00:00+00:00' both return {code: internal_error, message: 'Unexpected TypeError...', hint: 'Report it to the user with the id; do not retry with the same inputs.', details.error_type: TypeError}. The server log says 'Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware timestamps' (resolve_end_train).
- '2024-04-09' works. create_cv accepts initial_train_size with 'Z' or '+00:00'.
- On naive data, the zoned test_size is also internal_error, while create_cv answers invalid_argument '`initial_train_size` has a time zone (UTC), but the index has none. Use a date without time zone.'
findings.expected: forecast should read a test_size date with a time zone the way create_cv reads initial_train_size: accepted on tz-aware data, or an invalid_argument on field test_size saying to drop the zone. Never internal_error.
findings.agent_impact: SKILL.md tells the agent to pass the ISO 8601 date the test set starts at. On UTC data the agent naturally writes it as the data does, with 'Z'. It then gets an internal_error that tells it not to retry, so it reports a server bug instead of dropping the zone.

findings.title: The first get_code of a session waits about 20 s for a running ForecasterStats backtest, although SKILL.md says the read tools answer during long runs
findings.input: g_gaps/data/monthly_20y.csv. profile(target='y') -> plan(steps=12, forecaster='ForecasterStats') -> create_cv(initial_train_size=180, fold_stride=6) (10 folds) -> backtest(cv_id). 2 s later, concurrently: list_objects, describe_object(plan), get_code(cv). Control: a second server where get_code(plan) is called once before the backtest.
findings.observed:
- First server, during the backtest: list_objects answers in 0.0 to 0.2 s and describe_object in 0.0 to 0.1 s.
- get_code(cv) answers only after 19.3 to 19.4 s; the backtest ends at 21.4 to 21.7 s. get_code sends no progress meanwhile.
- Control server: the same get_code during the backtest answers in 0.1 s.
- The same happened with get_code(plan) during a Stats compare (answered when the first candidate ended).
- During a RandomForest backtest, the first get_code took 1.6 s.
findings.expected: Per SKILL.md ('Meanwhile only the read tools (get_code, get_failure, list_objects, describe_object) answer'), get_code should answer within a second or two during the run, like the other read tools.
findings.agent_impact: An agent that shows the user the code (or checks a plan's script) while a long ForecasterStats backtest or compare runs is told this answers at once. Instead it blocks for the whole run with no progress, which risks a client request timeout and leaves the agent waiting on a call it expected to be instant.

verdicts.title: ForecasterDirectMultiVariate keeps the estimator chosen for the pooled series (LGBMRegressor, '288 observations'); its backtest model learns nothing and repeats the same predictions in every fold

votes.reason: Script printed REPRODUCED: the DMV plan keeps 'Estimator: LGBMRegressor' with the profile reason '288 observations pooled across 3 series', the backtest predictions are identical in folds 0, 1 and 2 (62.421, 62.675, 62.688, 62.504), backtest MASE 3.5872, and compare on the same folds gives dmv_ridge 0.4877 against dmv_plan_estimator 3.5872. There are no notices at plan or create_cv, and only MetricReferenceNotice and MetricUnitNotice at backtest. In source, plan() deliberately recomputes the estimator when the task type changes (multi_series to multivariate), but it passes data_profile.n_total_observations (the pooled count) to select_estimator_and_candidates, whose rule (forecaster_selection.py:177, '< 250 -> Ridge') is about training rows. ForecasterDirectMultiVariate trains on one row per date (span_index_length 96), so the recomputation answers the wrong question. Nothing in SKILL.md, tool_catalog.md or docs/ documents a pooled count for DMV. It is not a duplicate of V01..V34: V01 is XGB in the default compare, not DMV's estimator. An agent following SKILL.md leaves the estimator to the rules and would report MASE 3.59 for a user who asked for DMV.
votes.covered_by_test: None. tests/test_assistant_plan.py::test_plan_multi_series_forecaster_when_wide_data_has_several_series only asserts plan.forecaster == 'ForecasterDirectMultiVariate'. No test checks the estimator chosen for a multivariate plan.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/assistant.py:1088-1095: when the task type changes to 'multivariate', the estimator is recomputed with n_obs_total = data_profile.n_total_observations (pooled across series). Fix: for task_type 'multivariate', pass data_profile.span_index_length (one row per date) to select_estimator_and_candidates, and build the plan's estimator reason from that count rather than reusing the profile's pooled reason (explanation.py:306).

The backtest predictions are the same in folds 0, 1 and 2 (62.421, 62.675, ...), which means the model is constant. Backtest MASE is 3.587, against 0.4877 for DMV+Ridge on the same folds. Plan, create_cv and backtest give no notice. In the source, a forecaster override that changes the task type ('multivariate', _constants.py:104) recomputes the estimator, but it uses data_profile.n_total_observations. That number pools all series, while ForecasterDirectMultiVariate trains on one row per date (96 here, so the <250 rule would pick Ridge). SKILL.md does not document this, and it duplicates none of V01..V34 (V29 is about kwargs dropped on an estimator change). An agent that follows SKILL.md leaves the estimator to the rules and reports MASE 3.59 for the forecaster the user asked for.

votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/assistant.py:1088 (n_obs_total = data_profile.n_total_observations passed to select_estimator_and_candidates at :1092 for the 'multivariate' task); the same pooled count is in the reason at skforecast_ai/recommendation/explanation.py:306. Fix: when the task type is 'multivariate', pass data_profile.span_index_length (rows per date) to the estimator rule and to the explanation, so DMV on 96 dates gets Ridge. Optionally add a plan notice when a gradient boosting estimator has fewer training rows than it needs to split.

verdicts.title: Long data whose series ids are numbers ('001', '002', '010' or 1, 2, 10) fails every backtest, forecast and compare with execution_failed KeyError: 1, and the zero padding is lost

votes.reason: Script printed REPRODUCED. Padded ids '001','002','010' are profiled as series '1','2','10' with no notices. backtest and forecast return execution_failed with field and hint null, compare returns all_candidates_failed, get_failure shows 'KeyError: 1', and the get_code script fails the same way when run standalone. Letter ids run fine. I reproduced it through the Python API too (forecast_code script, Ridge): the KeyError comes from skforecast 0.26 _forecaster_recursive_multiseries.py:1208. There encoding_mapping_ is built with str(level) keys (line 1519) but looked up by the integer series name that reshape_series_long_to_dict produced from the int-typed id column. skforecast-ai reads the CSV without a dtype for series_id_column (zeros lost) and renders reshape_series_long_to_dict on those ints. The codebase clearly expects integer ids (tests/test_load_exog.py::test_load_exog_output_when_integer_series_ids, tests/tests_profiling/test_series_ending_early.py), and nothing documents them as unsupported. It is not a duplicate of V01..V34 (V13 is integer dates, V22 is target list plus id column). The workflow dead-ends with no actionable hint, so an agent cannot propose the fix.
votes.covered_by_test: None. No end-to-end test runs long data with numeric series ids. Fixtures use text ids ('series', 'store' with letters), and test_load_exog only covers reading integer ids in the future exog file.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/rendering/_helpers.py:1395-1430 (_emit_reshape_series_long_to_dict) hands integer series ids to skforecast, whose encoding_mapping_ uses str keys. skforecast_ai/_utils.py:1026 (read_csv_with_dialect) reads the id column as int, dropping zero padding. Fix: read series_id_column with dtype=str both when profiling and in the emitted pd.read_csv, so '001' is kept, or emit data[series_id] = data[series_id].astype(str) before the reshape in both the script and the exec path.

votes.reason: I ran the script and got the same result. With ids '001','002','010' the profile names the series '1','2','10'. backtest and forecast return execution_failed, compare returns all_candidates_failed, and get_failure shows 'KeyError: 1'; letter ids run fine. I rendered the script with the Python API and ran it on its own: it fails at forecaster.fit in skforecast _forecaster_recursive_multiseries.py:1208 (encoding_mapping_[series_name_k], KeyError: 1). The cause is that the long CSV is read with pd.read_csv and no dtype for the id column, so the ids become integers and the zero padding is lost. Neither SKILL.md nor docs/ asks for text ids, no test covers numeric ids, and it duplicates none of V01..V34 (V22 is about a target list combined with series_id_column). The workflow dead-ends on a very common data shape, and get_failure gives no clue that the ids are the cause.
votes.covered_by_test: none (no test in tests/ or tests/tests_mcp/ profiles or runs long data with numeric or zero-padded series ids)
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/rendering/_helpers.py:540 (long-format read_csv rendered without dtype for the series id column) and skforecast_ai/_utils.py:894 (the profile reads the CSV the same way, so it names the series '1', '2', '10'). Fix: read series_id_column as text in profiling and in the generated script (dtype={series_id_column: str}), which keeps '001' and gives skforecast string keys. Failing that, check before running that the ids are text and raise invalid_argument on series_id_column with a hint.

verdicts.title: A series too short for the plan is silently left out of a multi-series backtest (empty row, average over the others, no notice), then forecast of the same plan fails on it

votes.reason: Script printed REPRODUCED. The profile and plan notice reads 'Short series: only 20 observations' without naming S02, and create_cv has no notice. backtest returns only the metric notices, and its 'Results (average across series)' covers S01 and S10, while forecast of the same plan is insufficient_data naming 'S02': 20. Partly documented intent: _last_window.py validate_series_lengths docstring and tests/test_validate_series_lengths.py::test_validate_series_lengths_passes_when_whole_data_and_series_starts_late say backtesting deliberately lets through a late-starting series 'left out of the first folds by skforecast'. SKILL.md also says 'a series without data in a fold is not forecast in it'. That intent covers a series missing from some folds. Here S02 has fewer values (20) over the whole data than the window (24), so it can never be forecast in any fold, and the check (`if not whole_data and ...`) skips exactly that case with no notice. Weaker than claimed: my verify script (verify/g03_summaries.py) shows the backtest summary's <evaluation_metrics> block does list S02 with NaN, so an agent reading the summary sees that S02 has no values. It just gets no reason, and the 'average across series' line silently excludes it. Not a duplicate of V01..V34 (V16 is a missing target inside a test fold). Kept as low-severity friction, not a wrong result.
votes.covered_by_test: tests/test_validate_series_lengths.py::test_validate_series_lengths_passes_when_whole_data_and_series_starts_late accepts a short late series in backtesting (whole_data=True), but its series is still forecastable in later folds. No test covers a series shorter than the window over the whole data, so the bad case is accepted, not asserted against.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/_last_window.py:816 (`if not whole_data and not foundation and length <= window`) skips every short series in backtesting, called from skforecast_ai/assistant.py:3236-3241. Fix: in whole_data mode, still detect series whose whole span is <= window and either raise insufficient_data as forecast does, or emit a notice naming them ('never forecast in any fold'). Also name the series in the DataProfileWarning of profiling/data_profile.py:2960.

votes.reason: I ran the script and got the same result. The profile and plan notice says 'Short series: only 20 observations' without naming the series, and create_cv has no notice. The backtest succeeds, the S02 row of files.metrics is all NaN, the predictions have no S02 rows, and the summary still says 'Results (average across series)' with an average over S01 and S10 only. forecast of the same plan then fails with insufficient_data naming 'S02': 20. In the source, validate_series_lengths with whole_data=True deliberately skips the length check in backtesting. Its docstring gives the reason: 'a series that starts late is left out of the first folds by skforecast'. Here S02 (20 values, window 24) is left out of every fold, a case the design does not cover. tests/test_validate_series_lengths.py::test_validate_series_lengths_passes_when_whole_data_and_series_starts_late accepts the pass, which does not refute the finding. Two things lower the impact: the NaN row is visible in the file SKILL.md tells the agent to read, and forecast fails with a clear error. Still, the average 'across series' and the missing notice let the agent present a backtest as the accuracy of a plan that can never forecast one store. It duplicates none of V01..V34 (V30 is a single-series hold-out with execution_failed).
votes.covered_by_test: tests/test_validate_series_lengths.py::test_validate_series_lengths_passes_when_whole_data_and_series_starts_late accepts a late-starting series in backtesting. No test covers a series that is too short in every fold.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/_last_window.py:816 (`if not whole_data and not foundation and length <= window`: in backtesting a series is never checked against the window), and skforecast_ai/execution/backtesting_runner.py:212 (the average label ignores NaN rows). Fix: in backtesting, raise insufficient_data (or emit a notice naming the series) when a series' span never exceeds the forecaster window by the last training end of the last fold, as forecast already does. The multi-series summary should say 'average across N of M series' when a row has no metrics.

verdicts.title: forecast(test_size=<ISO date with a time zone>) is an internal_error TypeError ('do not retry'), on tz-aware and naive data alike

votes.reason: Script printed REPRODUCED. On both UTC and naive data, forecast(test_size='2024-04-09T00:00:00Z' or '+00:00') returns internal_error TypeError with the 'do not retry' hint, and the server log shows 'Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware timestamps' at data_profile.py:4047 in resolve_end_train. The same date without a zone works. create_cv accepts the zoned date on UTC data and answers a clear invalid_argument on naive data. Source: assistant.py:4498 calls resolve_end_train with span_start_date ('2024-03-20', naive) and never passes the profile's time_zone ('UTC'). training_end(test_size, index.tz=None) then returns a tz-aware Timestamp, and the range comparison at line 4047 sits outside the try that converts TypeError into InvalidInputError. SKILL.md tells the agent to pass 'the ISO 8601 date the test set starts at', and a 'Z' suffix is valid ISO 8601. Nothing documents that zones are refused. Not a duplicate of V01..V34.
votes.covered_by_test: None. tests/tests_profiling/test_resolve_end_train.py::test_resolve_end_train_output_when_hourly_data covers a start_date carrying an offset and a test_size without a zone. It covers neither the server's real call (naive span_start_date plus a separate time_zone) nor a test_size with a zone. tests/tests_mcp/test_tool_forecast.py only uses '2007-07-01'.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/assistant.py:4498-4503 calls resolve_end_train without the data's time_zone. skforecast_ai/profiling/data_profile.py:4043-4047 compares the parsed test_size with a naive rebuilt index outside the try/except. Fix: pass data_profile.time_zone and build the index as create_cv does (_aware_index), convert a zoned test_size to the data's zone, and raise InvalidInputError(field='test_size') when the data has no zone ('drop the time zone'), as create_cv does.

votes.reason: I ran the script and got the same result. On the UTC data, forecast with test_size '2024-04-09T00:00:00Z' or '+00:00' returns internal_error TypeError 'Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware timestamps', with the hint 'do not retry with the same inputs'. The naive data gives the same error, while create_cv handles zoned dates (it accepts them, or answers invalid_argument on naive data). The traceback points at resolve_end_train. That function rebuilds the index naive from span_start_date and is given no time zone (assistant.py:4498). training_end only localizes naive dates, and the comparison at line 4047 sits outside the try, so the TypeError escapes. SKILL.md asks for 'the ISO 8601 date the test set starts at', and the data itself is written with 'Z'. tests/test_assistant_forecast.py::test_forecast_evaluation_mode_with_time_zone covers only an integer test_size on tz-aware data. It duplicates none of V01..V34.
votes.covered_by_test: none. tests/test_assistant_forecast.py::test_forecast_evaluation_mode_with_time_zone and test_forecast_evaluation_mode_when_hourly_data_and_test_size_int use an integer test_size only.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/profiling/data_profile.py:4047 (the comparison of a tz-aware test_size with the naive index rebuilt at :4008, outside the try of :4039), called from skforecast_ai/assistant.py:4498 without the time zone of the data. Fix: pass DataProfile.time_zone to resolve_end_train and place a zoned date on the aware index as create_cv does (_aware_index in recommendation/backtesting.py). On naive data, raise InvalidInputError on field test_size saying to drop the zone; never let the TypeError escape.

verdicts.title: The first get_code of a session waits about 20 s for a running ForecasterStats backtest, although SKILL.md says the read tools answer during long runs

votes.reason: Script printed REPRODUCED. During a 10-fold ForecasterStats backtest, list_objects and describe_object answered in 0.1 s, but the first get_code answered after 22.5 s (the backtest ended at 24.6 s). In the control, where get_code had already run once, it answered in 0.1 s. My verify script (verify/g05_event_loop_blocked.py) shows it is worse than reported: a list_objects sent 1 s after that first get_code also waits until 23.5 s, so get_code blocks the server's whole event loop, not only itself. Cause in source: get_code is an async tool that calls _requirements() synchronously on the event loop. The first call runs the uncached _distributions() -> importlib.metadata.packages_distributions(), which scans every installed distribution: about 1.5 s alone, stretched to about 20 s by contention for the Python global interpreter lock (GIL) with the CPU-bound Stats thread. This contradicts SKILL.md ('Meanwhile only the read tools (get_code, get_failure, list_objects, describe_object) answer') and stalls progress notifications. It only hits the first get_code of a process during a run that holds the GIL, so the frequency is low. Not a duplicate of V01..V34 (V26 is about cancelling a huge estimator).
votes.covered_by_test: None. tests/tests_mcp/test_concurrency.py checks that executions do not overlap. tests/tests_mcp/test_undeclared_distributions.py tests _distributions() output only. No test calls a read tool during a long run.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/mcp/server.py:2673 (get_code calls _requirements synchronously on the event loop), whose first call runs server.py:1293 metadata.packages_distributions() uncached. Fix: warm _distributions() at server start (for example in the preload thread of mcp/_preload.py), or compute requirements with anyio.to_thread.run_sync so the event loop and the other read tools are never blocked.

votes.reason: I ran the script and got the same result: the first get_code answered after 21.5 s (the backtest ended at 23.6 s), list_objects and describe_object after 0.0 s, and the control after 0.1 s. Cause: get_code is an async tool that calls _requirements on the event loop. On first use, _distributions() (lru_cache) runs a cold importlib.metadata.packages_distributions() scan. Alone that scan took 1.26 s on this machine. With one CPU-bound thread holding the GIL it took 29 s (convoy effect), as it does next to the ForecasterStats worker thread. It is also worse than reported. My check in reports/mcp-blackbox-audit/verify/g05_event_loop_blocked.py sent get_code at 2 s and list_objects at 3 s: list_objects answered only at 22.6 s, together with get_code. So the whole event loop stalls, including the 5 s progress heartbeats. Since then that file has been overwritten on disk by a similar check that tests the same thing. This contradicts the SKILL.md promise that the read tools answer during a long call, and it duplicates none of V01..V34 (V26 is about non-read tools behind an endless run). Impact stays limited: it happens once per process, lasts about 20 to 30 s, and only when get_code runs alongside a CPU-bound run.
votes.covered_by_test: none. tests/tests_mcp/test_concurrency.py and test_heartbeat.py do not run a read tool during a run, and test_undeclared_distributions.py clears the cache only to test the mapping.
votes.root_cause: skforecast_ai/mcp/server.py:2673 (get_code calls _requirements on the event loop), which at server.py:1371 calls _distributions(), whose cold metadata.packages_distributions() scan (server.py:1293) runs on the event loop thread. Fix: warm _distributions() in the background preload at startup (mcp/_preload.py), or run _requirements through anyio.to_thread.run_sync, so the scan never blocks the event loop.
